name: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated
executive_summary: UnitedHealth Group remains the dominant US integrated payer–provider platform, combining UnitedHealthcare insurance with Optum’s pharmacy, data and care-delivery businesses. The quantitative screen rates the name a buy on cheapness, dividend, GARP and risk metrics (P/E 25.8, FCF yield 6.7%, PEG 0.42, yield 2.3%), though deep-value and quality screens fail on leverage and thin reported margins. FY2025 was a trough year—consolidated net earnings fell to $12.1bn (10-K parent schedule) on Brazil/South America exit losses, Optum Health operating losses and Medicare medical-cost pressure—yet H1 2026 filings show a sharp interim recovery, with net earnings of $12.2bn (+21% YoY) and medical care ratio (MCR) improving to 85.3% from 87.1%. The central debate is whether margin repair and portfolio reshaping (Medicare Advantage exits, South America divestiture, Optum realignment) can restore earnings power fast enough to justify a premium multiple, against heavy CMS exposure (44% of premium revenue), ongoing DOJ/IRS actions and reputational fallout from the December 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.
investment_thesis:
For a value-oriented investor, UNH offers a scaled franchise trading below its historical earnings peak but with identifiable trough dynamics and screen-supported cash-return attributes. The buy signal rests on four pillars visible in the source pack.

**Scale and integration.** Per the FY2025 10-K segment table, consolidated revenues reached $447.6bn (+12% YoY from $400.3bn), with UnitedHealthcare premiums of $352.2bn and Optum revenues of $270.6bn (before eliminations). CMS premium revenue rose to 44% of consolidated premiums, underscoring government-program scale but also concentration risk.

**Trough-to-recovery earnings arc.** Reported net earnings declined from $22.4bn (2023) to $14.4bn (2024) to $12.1bn (2025), driven by an $8.3bn Brazil disposal loss in 2024, $950m of 2025 held-for-sale charges, and UnitedHealthcare segment earnings from operations collapsing from $15.6bn to $9.4bn. Optum Health swung from $7.8bn operating profit (2024) to a $278m loss (2025). Interim filings indicate stabilisation: H1 2026 net earnings of $12.2bn versus $10.0bn in H1 2025; Q2 2026 diluted EPS of $6.04 versus $3.74; Q2 MCR of 86.7% versus 89.4%.

**Cash generation and shareholder returns.** Screen FCF of ~$24.3bn (TTM) and filing-confirmed capital return discipline support the dividend and GARP model passes. FY2025 share repurchases totalled $5.5bn (12m shares at $454.82 average); dividends were raised to an $8.84 annual rate. H1 2026 operating cash flow was $20.0bn per the Q2 2026 10-Q.

**Valuation hook.** At P/E 25.8 and PEG 0.42, the market prices a partial recovery rather than a full re-rating to pre-2024 peaks (diluted EPS $23.86 in 2023). If H1 2026 run-rate earnings persist, the screen’s growth input (61.5%) may reflect rebound arithmetic rather than structural growth—a point requiring verification, but consistent with a GARP entry rather than deep value.
financial_review:
**Annual results (10-K, filed 27 Feb 2025 for FY2024; 2 Mar 2026 for FY2025)**

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Source |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Total revenues | $371.6bn | $400.3bn | $447.6bn | 10-K segment tables |
| Earnings from operations | $32.4bn | $32.3bn | $19.0bn | 10-K segment tables |
| Net earnings | $22.4bn | $14.4bn | $12.1bn | 10-K Schedule I (parent) |
| Diluted EPS | $23.86 | $15.51 | $13.23 | Yahoo fallback — consolidated EPS not in truncated 10-K body extract |
| Total assets | $273.7bn | $298.3bn | $309.6bn | 10-K segment tables |
| CMS premium share | 40% | 40% | 44% | 10-K Note 15 |

FY2024 earnings were depressed by a $7.1bn Brazil sale loss and $1.2bn reclassification of remaining South American operations to held-for-sale (10-K Note 13/14). FY2025 added $950m of held-for-sale operating losses, a $265m disposal loss, and Optum Health’s first annual operating loss. UnitedHealthcare earnings from operations fell 40% YoY to $9.4bn, reflecting Medicare Advantage funding pressure and elevated medical costs referenced in MD&A.

Consolidated operating cash flow of $19.7bn and free cash flow of $16.1bn for FY2025 are cited from `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo fallback—the 10-K body extract contains parent-company cash flows of $13.3bn only, not consolidated). FY2025 FCF declined from $20.7bn in FY2024, consistent with lower earnings and continued M&A ($4.8bn of acquisitions in 2025 per 10-K Note 13). Balance-sheet leverage remains elevated: total debt of ~$78.4bn at 31 Dec 2025 (Yahoo fallback; filing shows $72.3bn long-term plus $6.1bn current maturities in Q2 2026 10-Q), debt/equity 69% per screen, current ratio 0.79. Statutory capital at regulated subsidiaries was $43.1bn versus required $23.2bn (10-K Note 10)—adequate but dividend upstream remains subject to regulatory approval.

**Interim results (10-Q)**

*Q3 2025 (filed 28 Oct 2025):* Nine-month net earnings $12.6bn versus $9.5bn in 9M 2024; Q3 alone was weak at $2.5bn net earnings and $2.59 diluted EPS, with Q3 MCR elevated on premium growth and medical costs of $80.0bn versus $66.0bn YoY.

*Q2 2026 (filed 10 Aug 2026):* Strongest recent quarter. Q2 revenues $112.0bn (+0.4% YoY); net earnings $5.7bn (+59%); diluted EPS $6.04 (+61%). Six-month revenues $223.8bn (+1.2%); net earnings $12.2bn (+21%); diluted EPS $12.94 (+22%). H1 MCR 85.3% vs 87.1%. H1 operating cash flow $20.0bn vs $12.6bn prior year—a material working-capital/medical-payables swing worth monitoring. Cash rose to $28.6bn from $24.4bn at year-end; total debt fell to ~$73.3bn.

*Q1 2026 (filed 5 May 2026):* Q1 net earnings $6.5bn (flat YoY); diluted EPS $6.90 vs $6.85; revenues $111.7bn (+2.0%).

MD&A in the Q2 2026 10-Q states Medicare Advantage membership is contracting through 2026 as the company exits certain markets and reprices benefits, and flags continued Medicaid behavioural/pharmacy cost pressures. Optum Financial (including Optum Bank) moved from Optum Health to Optum Insight effective 1 Jan 2026, with prior periods to be recast.

**Gaps:** Consolidated income-statement and cash-flow tables for FY2023–FY2025 are truncated in the 10-K body extracts; annual EPS and consolidated cash flows rely partly on Yahoo fallback or Schedule I net earnings. Nine of ten indexed 8-K filings have no body extract. No going-concern language appears in available filing text.
risks_and_flags:
**Regulatory and reimbursement.** CMS premium concentration at 44% creates direct exposure to Medicare Advantage rate cuts, RADV audit clawbacks, and coding compliance. The 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q disclose an active DOJ False Claims Act case on risk-adjustment submissions; a Special Master recommended summary judgment for UNH in March 2025, but the DOJ has asked the court to reject that report—outcome cannot be reasonably estimated. Broad government investigations across CMS, OIG, DOJ, SEC and IRS are routine but ongoing.

**Medical cost and membership.** Q2 2026 MD&A confirms continued Medicare Advantage membership contraction and Optum Health care-arrangement shrinkage through 2026. Elevated Medicaid behavioural, pharmacy and home-health utilisation creates a timing mismatch with state rate updates. MCR improvement in H1 2026 is encouraging but may reflect mix shift from exits as much as underlying trend moderation.

**Tax.** On 6 Mar 2026 the company received IRS Notices of Proposed Adjustment for 2017–2020 intercompany transfer pricing, with potential extension to later years (Q2 2026 10-Q). Reserves are deemed adequate, but the dispute could be material.

**Leverage and liquidity.** Screen current ratio 0.79 and debt/equity 69% fail multiple financial-health models. Credit ratings cited in Q2 2026 MD&A show negative outlooks on senior unsecured debt (A2/A+/A-). Put/call obligations on unconsolidated businesses estimated at $4.8bn (10-K Note 12). Negative tangible book value (~$36.9bn per Yahoo) reflects goodwill-heavy balance sheet.

**Governance and reputational.** CEO transition: Stephen Hemsley returned as Chair and CEO (10-K signed March 2026); Wayne DeVeydt appointed CFO (effective September 2025 per 10-K exhibits). The December 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson and subsequent Luigi Mangione guilty plea (August 2026 news) sustain elevated public scrutiny of insurer practices.

**Portfolio execution.** Optum Health’s FY2025 operating loss and South America exit losses highlight execution risk in portfolio reshaping. A $1.7bn gain from deconsolidation of a business in Q4 2025 (10-K Note 14) adds complexity to earnings quality assessment—partially captured by the screen’s Earnings Quality model pass, but Piotroski F-Score of 6/9 failed.
